# linux_file_block (Resource)

Manages a block of lines between two marker lines in a file, like Ansible's `blockinfile`. The rest of the file is left untouched. Changes made to the block outside of Terraform show up in the plan. Destroying the resource removes the block and its markers.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_file_block" "deploy_match" {
  path    = "/etc/ssh/sshd_config"
  marker  = "# {mark} deploy user"
  content = <<-EOT
    Match User deploy
        PasswordAuthentication no
        X11Forwarding no
  EOT
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) Lines kept between the markers.
- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file.

### Optional

- `create` (Boolean) Create the file, with mode `0644`, when it does not exist. Otherwise a missing file is an error. Defaults to `false`.
- `insert_after` (String) Regular expression: insert the block after the last line matching it. Without a match, or when unset, the block goes at the end of the file.
- `insert_before` (String) Regular expression: insert the block before the first line matching it. Use `.*` for the beginning of the file.
- `marker` (String) Marker line, where `{mark}` becomes `BEGIN` and `END`. Give each block of a file its own marker, such as `# {mark} nginx upstreams`. Defaults to `# {mark} TERRAFORM MANAGED BLOCK`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Random identifier.
